edges.description: Constitutive JAK-STAT signaling in transformed hematopoietic stem cells drives clonal expansion across one or more myeloid lineages and megakaryocytes.
Clonal overproduction and intrinsic functional activation of platelets and leukocytes promote multicellular aggregation and vascular endothelial activation.
Clonal megakaryocytic hyperplasia directly increases circulating platelet production.
Clonal granulocytic and myeloid expansion elevates total circulating leukocyte counts in a subset of patients.
Extramedullary hematopoiesis and splenic sequestration of clonal myeloid populations produce progressive, sometimes bulky splenomegaly.
Clonal myeloproliferation and associated inflammatory cytokine signaling contribute to constitutional symptom burden including fatigue.
Intravascular platelet-leukocyte aggregation, endothelial activation, and coagulation cascade activation directly precipitate arterial and venous thrombosis.
Qualitative platelet dysfunction, extreme thrombocytosis or cytopenias, and antithrombotic exposure contribute to clinically significant bleeding events in MPN-U.
Blast-phase expansion of ≥20% myeloid blasts manifests clinically as secondary acute myeloid leukemia.

nodes.description: Acquired somatic gain-of-function driver mutations affecting JAK2, CALR, or MPL arise in a hematopoietic stem cell in the bone marrow and establish clonal hematopoiesis, including early or unclassifiable presentations with low variant allele frequencies. Activating JAK2 and MPL variants directly increase non-receptor tyrosine kinase and thrombopoietin cytokine receptor activity, respectively, whereas mutant CALR lacks intrinsic kinase or receptor activity and acts by binding and constitutively activating the thrombopoietin receptor MPL.
